newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Montenegrin ruling party wins polls - official.
newsitem.headline: Montenegrin ruling party wins polls - official.

text.p: The ruling Democratic Party of Socialists (DPS) of Montenegro won a resounding victory at Sunday's republican parliamentary elections, the republican election commission said on Tuesday.

"The DPS got... 45 seats in the (71-seat) Montenegrin assembly, the opposition coalition National Unity won 19 seats," Yugoslav news agency Tanjug quoted election commission chairman Marko Dakic as saying.
The Moslem Party of Democratic Action won three seats, the Democratic Alliance of Montenegro and the Democratic Union of Albanians got two seats each, Dakic said.
He said the turnout stood at 67.1 percent.
The count for the 138-seat federal parliament elections where Montenegrins have 30 seats was not completed but the DPS was also expected to win there.

The DPS votes together with the allied Serbian left coalition, which has claimed almost two thirds of seats, is expected to give Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic firm control of the federal parliament.
This majority will enable Milosevic, who is widely considered the real power-broker in Yugoslavia, to move into the post of federal president vested with sweeping executive powers.
